To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
UV-B radiation causes a reduction in the rate of photosynthesis in oilseed rape, which is due to a reduction in the amount of Rubisco, the enzyme that fixes CO 2 into sugar.

UV-B radiation causes decreases in the activity and content of the enzyme Rubisco in leaves of Brassica napus, and that these decreases in enzyme activity and content are the major cause of UV-B-induced inhibition of CO2 fixation in these plants.
UV‐B radiation reduced the rate of CO2 assimilation in leaves of two cultivars of B. napus, and that the reduction in photosynthesis was due to a loss of Rubisco.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of ultraviolet radiation (UV) on photosynthesis and growth of plants in the field and in the laboratory.
understanding the effects of UV radiation on photosynthesis and the mechanisms of photosynthetic inhibition.
the effects of UV-B radiation (280-320 nm) on the photosynthetic apparatus in the leaves of two cultivars of oil-seed rape (Brassicaceae).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
UV-B inhibits photosynthesis of oilseed rape by reducing the capacity for CO 2 assimlation.
the UV-B effects on the photosynthetic apparatus of oilseed rape were primarily a result of the reduction in the activity of the primary carboxylation enzyme, Rubisco.
UV-B inhibition of leaf CO 2 assimilatio n in B. napus is caused by a decrease in Rubisco content and carboxylation velocity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
exposure to UV-B causes a loss of Rubisco, which is accompanied by photodamage to PSII and a decrease in the rate of linear electron flow in one cultivar.
UV-B inhibition of photosynthesis was due to a combination of effects of UV-B on the photosynthetic apparatus and a reduction in the rate of Rubisco carboxylation.
UV‐B inhibits CO 2 assimilating enzymes, but not stomata, and that the inhibition of photosynthesis in some cultivars may also involve photoinhibition of photosystem II.

UV-B radiation can inhibit photosynthesis in plants.
